ai_patterns_removed: Yudhishthira's five-question rhetorical run converted into a named roll-call (Bhishma, Drona, Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, Vidura, the kings) so a first reader can tell who is being asked about
scripture vocatives modernized: 'O you of lotus-petal eyes' -> plain 'Tell us all that you said... Tell us every word'; Krishna's 'Hear, O king' -> 'Hear, then'; 'beneficial' -> 'meant for his good'
double-name confusion fixed: 'Kshattri, Vidura, their junior father' -> 'Vidura — the one they also called Kshattri — their father's younger brother' (Kshattri IS Vidura, not a second person)
'procured Kali to become his mother' unravelled so Kali reads as the fisher chief's daughter won for Shantanu, not as the goddess
translationese register of Bhishma's remembered history naturalized ('highly incensed' -> 'deeply angered'; 'the chief of the gods withheld rain' -> 'the king of the gods held back the rain')
close trimmed of its doubled summary (the file twice said the Pandavas now knew in full what they had known in outline) — one quiet close kept
child_friendly_changes: opener anchors sides and stakes: Upaplavya is the camp of the five Pandava brothers, Hastinapura the city of their cousins the Kauravas, and the mission was to win back the kingdom they had lost
Bhishma identified as the grandsire of the Kuru house, Drona as 'their old teacher of arms', Virata as king of the Matsyas, at first mention
Dhritarashtra and Gandhari identified as Duryodhana's own parents (blind king of the Kurus and his queen)
Vidura glossed as the brothers' uncle who grieved for them as though they were his own sons

Bhishma's vow-history stepped out in order (only son -> second wife Kali -> promise renouncing his own claim to the throne -> half-brother Vichitravirya set on the throne -> drought and sickness -> refusal) so a child can follow why the line mattered
risk: Bhishma's remembered history keeps every fact in the file's order: the father's fear that an only son would end the line, the vow that set aside his own throne-claim, Vichitravirya installed while Bhishma served under him, the withheld rain, the starving sick subjects begging him to take the crown, and the refusal 'keeping his vow' — the refusal line is now 'He refused. A vow, once taken, is kept.' Yudhishthira's 'You are our refuge, our lord, our guide' kept verbatim. The Kali gloss adds only that she was the fisher chief's daughter, which the story's own source excerpt states.

ai_patterns_removed: epithets trimmed from Arjuna's cry ('mighty-armed one, giver of fearlessness to your devotees' dropped), keeping its core: 'Krishna, Krishna! You alone are the rescue of those being burned!'

Arjuna's three stacked theological clauses naturalized one by one (first of beings / Lord above the nature he had made / living world deluded by his power of illusion / coming into the world to lift the earth's burden)

bare Sanskrit 'Only an astra can quell an astra' kept with an inline gloss ('only one divine weapon can turn aside another'); 'brahma weapon' explained as 'one of the great weapons of Brahma, the creator'
redundant waking beat compressed ('the camp woke to the worst news a camp can wake to' folded into the awakening)
child_friendly_changes: opening names the war (five Pandava brothers vs their cousins the Kauravas) and marks the raid as the night the fighting stopped, so the scene stands alone
Ashvatthama introduced as son of Drona, 'the master of weapons who had trained the princes of both houses to fight'
Draupadi glossed once as wife of the Pandava brothers
brahmin glossed at first mention ('the priestly class, the teachers and keepers of sacred learning')
touching water 'as the rite requires' kept without further gloss so the unfamiliar ritual stays concrete
risk: Ashvatthama's motive kept exactly as the file framed it ('meaning to do what would please his master') without naming the master, to avoid asserting anything about the master's state after the war. The night killing of Draupadi's sleeping sons, Krishna's promise ('I will wipe away this sorrow of yours, good lady... with the head of that unworthy son of a brahmin, the assailant who struck without warning'), the pursuit with Krishna driving, the weapon that 'He does not know how to recall', the water-rite counter, the meeting of the two fires, the three worlds in peril, and the withdrawal of both weapons at Krishna's word are preserved in order. Cross-file note: Krishna's comfort-promise here and Arjuna's sworn promise recalled in DKS_0447 both exist in the source (BP 1.7.15 and 1.7.53); neither was altered to fit the other.

ai_patterns_removed: 'as the old tellers would say' aside removed (the same device appears in DKS_0448 — a repetitive flourish across the wave)
the metaphor 'struck down by the very children he had killed' simplified to 'the crime against sleeping children had stripped it from him' so literal young readers are not confused
'the four-armed one' epithet for Krishna dropped from the judgment scene (plain 'Krishna')
ambiguous pronouns in the opening unravelled: the file's averted face and the captor who looked away are two people (Ashvatthama and Arjuna), now spelled out
duplicated 'heard Bhima's words and Draupadi's both' (the file said it twice) reduced to one beat
child_friendly_changes: opening recap added (Ashvatthama killed Draupadi's sleeping sons after the fighting; Arjuna hunted him down) so the story stands alone
Draupadi identified as wife of the Pandava brothers; Nakula and Sahadeva as the two youngest of the five brothers; Satyaki as Krishna's own kinsman
brahmin explained at the crux of the judgment: 'the priest and teacher was held sacred, and the law guarded even an unworthy son of such a house'
'Panchali' in Krishna's quoted judgment glossed in the same breath ('so all called her, for the land of her father, the king of Panchala')
Gautami kept with her file gloss ('devoted as she is to her husband')
risk: Krishna's ordinance is preserved in substance: 'A brahmin's unworthy son is not to be slain, yet an assailant deserves punishment. Both are my ordinances; uphold them. Keep the promise you made to your beloved, and satisfy Bhima, Panchali, and me.' Bhima's catalogue (the mad, the careless, the sleeping, children, women, the helpless), his 'slayer of his own kindred', Draupadi's plea that Drona lives on in his son and that Gautami not weep, the jewel cut 'along with the hair', the release from bonds, the driving from camp, and the no-cheering close are all intact. Krishna's 'Beloved' of the promise and Bhima's 'You swore to Draupadi' both refer to the same oath and were not harmonized beyond the existing glosses.

ai_patterns_removed: opening doublet removed — 'the compassion of the Lord toward his unalloyed devotees' and 'out of love for those who love him without reserve' said the same thing twice and are now one beat
devotional stacking in the request softened to one clause (mind resting on him in love, voice keeping his name, the Lord waiting beside him while the body is given up)
'as the old tellers would say' aside removed from the death sentence (duplicate device with DKS_0447)

'attributeless Brahman' rendered 'the formless Brahman, the eternal beyond every name and shape'; 'Primal Person' -> 'the first of beings'; 'the four-armed Krishna' -> 'the four-armed form of Krishna'
child_friendly_changes: opener identifies Bhishma as the grandsire of the Kuru house and names the war (Pandavas vs their cousins) so the arrow-bed scene stands alone
tamala glossed inline ('its leaves almost black'); Rajasuya glossed as 'the sacrifice that crowns a king'; solstice rendered 'the auspicious turn of the year'
the four ends of a human life listed plainly as 'duty, gain, love, and freedom'; dharma glossed as 'right living'
the leap-from-the-chariot memory keeps every element: chariot placed between the armies, his sworn word set aside, Bhishma's vow made true, armor shattered, bathed in blood
risk: The deathbed prayer keeps its meaning ('how the Lord bends down to those who love him without reserve... May he be my refuge') and the request that the God of gods wait beside him until the body is given up. The remembered visions stay in the file's order: the tamala-dark charioteer with sweat on his face, the leap from the chariot by 'Krishna, who had sworn he would not fight... to make true the vow of the old warrior who had pressed him to it', the Rajasuya with its gentle smile and loving glance, and the closing 'Him, the unborn, who dwells in the heart of every living being — on him let my love rest.' The drums played by gods and men together and the rites for the departed end the story as in the file. At 700 words the story sits at the top of the target band; the event (a deathbed recollection of a lifetime) earns the length.

ai_patterns_removed: alternate epic name 'Suyodhana' dropped — Duryodhana alone (one person under two names)

theological exposition de-duplicated: the earth's burden and its lifting were stated three times in the file and are now said once ('the war was his instrument; when it was done, the earth would stand lighter')
double harvest metaphor fixed — 'the ripening of their own evil counsel... ripened into the harvest that reaped them' is now a single ripening image
editorializing close softened: 'a quarrel that should never have been settled in blood' -> 'a quarrel that came at last to blood' (show, don't tell)
child_friendly_changes: the two armies glossed inline as 'the five sons of Pandu drawn up against the hundred sons of their uncle Dhritarashtra'
Karna, Dushasana, and Shakuni identified in passing as Duryodhana's great friend, his brother, and his scheming uncle
the unexplained dice reference anchored ('set ablaze years before by a game of dice') so a first reader can follow it
Uddhava's role kept with his file gloss (Krishna's companion and messenger across the years)
risk: Names and fates intact: Karna, Dushasana, and Shakuni 'stripped of fortune and of life by the fruit of their own counsel'; Duryodhana 'with his thigh broken and his followers fallen about him'; the trembling earth at the gathering, the quiet after the war, and Uddhava's refusal to rejoice or call the field a victory. The only interpretive layer touched is the file's own theological frame (the earth's burden lifted by Krishna's design, Kurukshetra as the appointed place), which is retained, not added.

ai_patterns_removed: epic-translation register naturalized across the three candidate speeches: 'endued with great might' and 'irresistible in battle' -> plain claims; 'that bull among monarchs' dropped; 'accoutred in armour of steel, mounted on a car unto which were yoked excellent steeds' -> 'wearing armor of steel, mounted on a chariot yoked with excellent horses'; 'the clatter of his car-wheels was as deep as the roar of mighty masses of clouds' -> plainer simile
archaic vocatives removed from Yudhishthira's and Krishna's lines ('ye have named... thy troops' -> 'you have named... your troops'; 'O king' -> 'King')
the opening seven-leaders list moved from quoted catalogue into narration, with 'akshauhini' explained as 'a full army of the old reckoning, with its chariots, elephants, cavalry, and foot'
'generalissimo' -> 'commander' in the close
lion-imagery said once instead of twice (the file stacked 'like a lion in his frame and his prowess, with leonine shoulders, arms, chest, and a voice like a lion's roar')
child_friendly_changes: opening anchors who and where: seven armies at Upaplavya, the camp of the Pandava brothers and their allies, choosing a leader for the coming war
Bhimasena glossed as 'their own brother Bhima' (one person, two names) at first mention in the list
Dhrishtadyumna identified as Drupada's son and Draupadi's brother before his fire-birth portrait
the Vedas rendered 'the sacred hymns'; Bharadwaja kept with his title 'the sage'; the elephant simile kept plain ('carried himself like a great elephant')
Bhishma's threat kept concrete ('like a fire whose flames are arrows'; arrows that 'strike with the force of the thunderbolt and fall like flames of fire')
risk: Every argument survives in order: Sahadeva on Virata (close kin, grief-shared, mighty, skilled, 'recover our share of the kingdom'); Nakula on Drupada (father-in-law, king of Panchala, beyond reproach in years/learning/constancy/family, weapons under the sage Bharadwaja, challenger of Drona and Bhishma, the penance moved by wrath for Drona's destruction); Arjuna on Dhrishtadyumna (sprung from penance and the sages' blessings, out of the sacrificial fire armed with bow and sword, armored, lion-built, impenetrable to weapons, truthful, passions under control, born for Drona's destruction, the one man who can withstand Bhishma of the great vows); and Krishna's approval naming 'Dhrishtadyumna, the chastiser of his foes.' Similes were reworded or trimmed, never facts; the fire-born destiny line and the quiet close ('The Pandavas had their commander, and the war had its shape') are retained.
